messages:
Frank: FYI — following up on the 503 incident postmortem. Need to lock owners for remediation items and agree on what we tell customers on the status page and via CS.
Erin: +1. I can take lead on customer-facing wording if we decide what level of detail to include.
Carla: For remediation owners: I propose splitting into infra, runtime, and ops runbook work.
Ben: Agree. I'll own the runtime optimization task (reduce KV cache eviction rate). ETA 3 weeks.
Alice: I'll take the ops runbook updates + playbook for on-call. ETA 1 week.
Dave: Infra task (investigate network egress queueing in region eu-west-1) — I'll own. ETA 2 weeks.
Frank: Great. Can we put these into a quick tracking table in the postmortem doc and make them visible to leadership and CS?
Erin: I'll draft a short table and ping you. Also we should flag recurring pattern: this is the third 503-type outage in the last 6 months with similar throughput surge + cache miss pattern. Might need a recurring incident pattern tracker.
Carla: Agreed. I'll add recurrence notes to the RCA and tag it for the reliability working group.
Ben: For customer comms: do we publish full RCA publicly or only send to affected customers? What's our policy currently?
Erin: Current practice is: brief status page incident summary, and post a public incident summary within 72 hours. Full RCA is shared with customers on request or when it's security-sensitive. We should decide if this RCA qualifies for public posting.
Frank: My read: this was operational, root cause is internal scaling/caching config. No customer data involved. I lean to posting a public summary once remediation owners are assigned and we have mitigations scheduled.
Alice: As CS, we prefer a shorter, clear status page blurb + a link to the postmortem (private until we've validated fixes). We don't want to commit to timelines beyond the remediation ETAs.
Erin: Draft status page blurb suggestion (for review):
```
Incident: Increased 5xx rate (503) impacting hosted API in eu-west-1.
Impact: Intermittent request failures for ~2 hours; retries restored service for most customers.
Work underway: We identified an interaction between request burst patterns and our KV cache eviction thresholds; infra and runtime teams have owners assigned and are implementing mitigations to reduce cache churn and improve throttling.
Next update: Postmortem with remediation plan to be published within 7 business days.
```
Carla: Suggest removing the engineering jargon in the public blurb: replace "KV cache eviction" with "internal caching layer".
Ben: Also change "throttling" to "traffic shaping"? Not necessary — I'd stick with plain language: "safeguards to better handle traffic spikes."
Erin: Updated blurb for customer-facing status page (final draft):
```
Incident: Intermittent request failures (503) in eu-west-1.
Impact: Some customers experienced failed API requests for ~2 hours; automatic retries restored service for most traffic.
What we found: A cascading effect between high burst traffic and our internal caching, causing temporary service overload.
What were doing: Teams have owners assigned to implement mitigations and safeguards to reduce cache churn and improve handling of traffic spikes.
When well follow up: A postmortem summary with remediation owners and timelines will be posted within 7 business days.
```
Frank: Good — Erin, please coordinate with CS to publish that on the status page after we confirm owners in the postmortem doc.
Erin: Will do. Action items recap:
- Ben: runtime mitigation — owner, ETA 3w.
- Dave: infra investigation & fix — owner, ETA 2w.
- Alice: ops runbook & playbook updates — owner, ETA 1w.
- Carla: add recurrence analysis & tag for reliability WG — owner, ETA 5 days.
- Erin: publish status page blurb once owners are confirmed, and post a summary in 7 business days — owner, ETA 1 day to publish initial blurb.
Frank: I'll create corresponding JIRA tickets and link them in the postmortem.
IncidentBot: A new postmortem doc has been created: /docs/postmortems/2024-07-27-503-eu-west-1.md
Ben: One more ask — let's add a metric to monitor: cache miss rate 95p over 1m, and an alert if burst > X rps sustained 30s.
Dave: I'll add the alert to infra monitoring and set a tentative threshold; will sync with Ben on exact numbers.
Alice: I'll update the on-call rota and runbook to include the new alert handling steps.
Carla: For RCA sharing policy: recommend we include a short public summary and link to the internal postmortem; share the full technical RCA with affected customers on request. If a customer requests the full RCA, CS will coordinate redaction and sign-off by eng.
Erin: Sounds good. I'll draft the CS template for customer notifications and share in #customer-success.
Frank: Thanks everyone. Please update the postmortem doc with the owners table + JIRA links by EOD tomorrow. We'll reconvene in the reliability WG next week if the recurrence analysis looks concerning.
Ben: Noted.
Dave: On it.
Alice: Will finish runbook update by EOD Friday.
Erin: Posting initial status page blurb in 30m (once Frank confirms owners are linked).
Frank: Confirmed — go ahead. :thumbsup:
